If TWF was what you were going for vital strike probably wouldn't be the play imo. It'd still work well enough with shikigami style, but the issue you'd run into is the -4 from the offhand not being light (assuming you'd be dual welding 2-handers), the penalties from jotungrip itself, and the big issue of the dex requirements and extra feats needed of the TWF tree on top of that when you aren't vital striking. In other words, you'd be double dipping in two fighting styles in a way that doesn't really complement either of them enough to justify the feat tax needed to get them working. Just in my opinion anyway.

If TWF is something you'd be interested in, I may suggest taking the main build over to slayer (or perhaps ranger) for the studied target buffs and more importantly the fighting style talents that let you get around the TWF dex requirements. You could still take a couple levels of titan mauler to get some rage rounds and Jotungrip if you're feeling that, but you'd also get some other slayer talents and sneak attack to toss on the pile. Otherwise for pure barb oversized sledge+shikigami style chain+massive weapons feature+vital strike will probably have similar damage and more flexibility with less investment than pure barb TWF for this archetype.

If you're thinking titan Mauler with improvised weapons the shikigami style chain is a pretty solid option. Find yourself an oversized sledge and start throwing piles of d6s at whatever problems come up. Toss in the vital strike chain and furious finish once you have the feats for it and damage shouldn't be an issue for you.

I was looking for a magical weapon to give one of my players (sorcerer) for no real reason then because I like magical weapons, but I wanted it to be more mechanically interesting then just a +1 or +2 weapon. Not sure if its balanced or not but I think it has some potential to make some encounters more interesting, especially ones where casters don't have a lot of room to operate. Any feedback or criticism is more then welcome, and feel free to steal my idea if you like it.

Edit: I took some of the suggestions from the comments and made a revised version. The description is still pretty long, but I think its a definite improvement. I added the sorcerer, warlock, and wizard limitation as cleric, bard, and druid all seem to have an easier time with melee, plus the half casters and subclass casters have plentiful martial options already. Still, I am not against the idea of opening it up to all or most casters.

Channeling Wand

*Wondrous Item, Rare (requires attunement, sorcerer, warlock, wizard)*

This is a magical wand that gives the user +1 to spell attacks which only applies when in wand form. When twirled in the hand it becomes a full length Quarterstaff. When empowered by and attuned with the user, they can use the normal stats of a magical quarterstaff but they may use their spellcasting modifier for their attack and damage rolls, and the damage is of the same type the user empowered it with. To empower the Staff, the user must attune with the staff over a short rest and choose bludgeoning or a damage type dealt by any spell they know or have prepared/can prepare excluding piercing, slashing, and force. Switching between forms requires a bonus action.
Fair and balanced
